question: The _________ key(s) acts as a toggle key.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Caps Lock and Insert.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Caps Lock:** The Caps Lock key acts as a toggle key. When you press it, it toggles the capital letter functionality on or off. If Caps Lock is on, all alphabetic characters are typed in uppercase until it is pressed again to turn it off.
 
• **Insert:** The Insert key is another toggle key. When activated, it toggles between the "Insert" mode, which allows you to insert text at the cursor, and the "Overwrite" mode, which overwrites existing text.
 
• **Toggle Keys:** Toggle keys are special keys on the keyboard that switch between two states each time they are pressed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shift Key:** The Shift key is not a toggle key; it works as a modifier key to temporarily change the function of another key when pressed.
 
• **Ctrl Key:** The Ctrl key is also a modifier key that works in combination with other keys to perform specific tasks and is not a toggle key.
 
• **Other Examples of Toggle Keys:** The Num Lock and Scroll Lock keys also function as toggle keys, turning specific features on or off.
